Description: This class represents a custom exception that can be thrown to indicate errors during a startup process, carrying an error code and an optional message.
This class represents a specific, incompatible version of the Java runtime, allowing for the definition of required major versions and optional constraints on minor and patch versions.

This class is designed to verify if the currently running Java version is compatible with eXist-db. It checks against a list of known incompatible Java versions and will raise an exception if an incompatible version is detected, ensuring the stability and integrity of the database.
This class manages a collection of file system paths that constitute a classpath, allowing for the addition of components and the retrieval of a custom class loader based on these paths.
This class serves as the primary class loader for the eXist system, enabling the dynamic addition of resource locations at runtime.
This class provides utility methods for performing reflective operations, specifically for invoking the main method of a class dynamically and managing a custom class loader.
This class is responsible for bootstrapping and configuring the eXist-db Java environment before the database starts, by orchestrating various setup tasks and resolving necessary configurations.
This class represents a custom exception that signals the intentional stopping of a process or operation.
Provides access to various sample data files and their corresponding metadata, such as streams and URLs, for use within the application.
This class acts as a factory for creating and managing stylesheet resolvers and compilers, with support for caching instances for reuse.

This interface defines a contract for resolving and compiling XSLT stylesheets, providing methods to obtain compiled `Templates` objects and `TransformerHandler` instances for applying transformations. It is designed to work with a `DBBroker` for stylesheet retrieval and supports custom error listeners.
This class acts as a resolver and compiler for XSLT stylesheets, managing the loading, compilation, and caching of `Templates` objects for efficient transformation processing.
This code defines an enumeration for categorizing different types of errors, specifically warning, error, and fatal.
This class serves as a listener for XSL transformation errors, allowing for configurable handling of warnings, errors, and fatal errors by either logging them or stopping the transformation process.
This class acts as an XML reader that utilizes a serializer to deliver database documents to a content handler, implementing the SAX XMLReader interface.

This class is responsible for providing a configurable way to obtain a TransformerFactory for XSLT transformations, allowing the specific implementation to be determined by configuration settings rather than being hardcoded.
This class resolves uniform resource identifiers (URIs) by interfacing with a database broker pool to locate and retrieve resources, supporting both database-internal paths and external URLs.
Provides utility methods for resolving URIs within XSLT processing, allowing for the retrieval of appropriate URI resolvers based on context.
This class represents an XML document residing within the eXist database, providing access to its broker and document information, and allowing for the configuration of input streams.
This class provides an XML document from the eXist database as a SAXSource, enabling it to be processed by XML parsers.
This class acts as a custom factory for creating XML-RPC types, specifically designed to support extended types when interacting with eXist-db.
This class is a container for a DocumentType and its associated count, designed to track the occurrences of specific document types.
This class is a private helper for tracking the number of references to a DocumentImpl object, allowing for efficient memory management.

This class acts as a listener that buffers and logs various events occurring during a restore operation, such as task start, descriptor processing, collection creation, resource restoration, skipped resources, informational messages, warnings, errors, and task completion.
This class implements the XML-RPC API for the eXist-db database, providing a wide range of methods for managing documents, collections, users, and executing queries.

This class acts as a factory for creating factories that produce request processors specifically designed for XML-RPC database interactions. It ensures that the correct processor factory is instantiated based on the requested class, managing its lifecycle.
This class registers public methods from a provided Java class as default XML-RPC handlers, enabling their invocation via XML-RPC without requiring explicit handler name mapping.
This interface defines a specialized function for handling XML-RPC server operations, focusing on converting database-related exceptions into EXistException types.

This interface defines a functional operation for XML-RPC servers, specifically handling database interactions by converting various exceptions into `EXistException` or `PermissionDeniedException` types.

This interface defines a functional contract for operations targeting XML-RPC server functionalities, specifically designed to process collections within a database transaction and handle various exceptions by converting them into a standardized EXistException type.

This interface represents a specialized function for handling XML-RPC server operations, primarily focused on converting database exceptions into specific EXistException types when executing compiled XQueries.
This class is responsible for serializing objects, specifically sub-classes of `Tuple`, into an XML format suitable for XML-RPC communication.
This abstract class serves as a container for cached query results, enabling retrieval of data in chunks and managing the lifecycle of the cached resource.
This class serves as a wrapper for `ContentFile` objects, providing caching capabilities and managing the lifecycle of the cached content, including its eventual return to a pool.
This factory is responsible for creating and initializing XML-RPC request handlers, specifically for eXist, ensuring each handler is properly set up.
This class provides a mechanism to store and retrieve query results, identified by unique integer IDs, for efficient caching and reuse.

This class acts as a container to store and cache the outcome of a query, allowing for later retrieval of the results or any associated errors. It is designed to hold a sequence of results or an exception, along with properties related to serialization and query execution time.
Serializes ACEAider objects into XML-RPC format.
This class parses XML-RPC types, specifically handling the structure of sub-classes of `Tuple`, by recursively processing XML elements to reconstruct tuple objects.
This class acts as a container to hold and cache the results of a query, allowing for later retrieval by the client and manages the cleanup of temporary files.
This class serves as an XML-RPC parser specifically designed to interpret and transform XML representations of ACEAider objects into their corresponding Java object structure.
This class represents and manipulates virtual storage addresses within a paged file system, encoding page numbers, tuple identifiers, and type indicators into a single 64-bit value.

This interface defines a collection of static constants used for configuring and signaling states within a broker pool, intended to declutter the main `BrokerPool` class by externalizing these values.
This interface defines a contract for checking if a sequence of characters matches a specific term or pattern.

This class provides utility methods for encoding and decoding information about node types and their storage size from a byte signature, which is stored as the first byte of node data in a persistent DOM.

This class is responsible for creating XML backups of the database. It can output backups to a directory or a zip file and ensures data consistency by preventing other transactions during the backup process.
This enum defines the possible states a BrokerPool can be in, ranging from initialization through operational status to various shutdown phases.
This class defines a set of enumerated event types used for managing the initialization and shutdown states of a system, including specific modes like multi-user mode.

This class acts as a publisher of system status updates. It allows for setting and updating the status, and notifies any registered observers of these changes. It also provides a mechanism to signal the termination of its reporting activity and ensures that any threads waiting on its status are released.
This enum defines the two possible states for a change: getting a resource or releasing it.
This class represents immutable information about a broker, storing its unique identifier and a reference count.
This class is used for tracing changes related to broker leases, specifically when brokers are acquired or released, and tracks their reference counts.
This class manages all instances of a database, providing functionality to configure, start, stop, and retrieve individual database instances, each with its own settings and resources.
This class defines the specification for a range index based on a qualified name (QName), storing the namespaces and name used to construct the QName.
This class represents an exception that aggregates multiple service-specific exceptions encountered within a broker pool, allowing for the reporting of all encountered errors.
This class encapsulates statistics related to a buffer, tracking its total size, current usage, and the number of page hits and failures.
This class implements a cache with a Last Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy, storing cacheable items and managing their lifecycle based on usage.
This interface defines the contract for objects that can be stored in a cache, requiring them to provide a unique key, manage a reference count, and support timestamping and pre-eviction cleanup.
This class tracks cache performance metrics such as hits, misses, and thrashing, and uses this information to determine if the cache needs to be resized to improve efficiency.
This class implements a cache that prioritizes keeping inner B-tree pages in memory while allowing leaf pages to be evicted based on usage.
This class implements a cache with a Least Reference Density (LRD) replacement policy, managing items based on their reference counts and age to optimize cache performance and prevent stale data.
This enum defines the distinct types of caches supported by the system: BTREE and DATA.
This interface defines the contract for cache implementations used to buffer btree and data pages, providing methods for adding, retrieving, removing, and managing cache items and their state.
This interface defines a contract for objects that can be cached and also indicates whether they represent an inner page within a B-tree structure.

This class implements a cache with a size-limited collection of items, prioritizing the eviction of less recently or less frequently used items to maintain performance. It manages items using reference counts and employs a GClock algorithm for item replacement when the cache is full.
This enum defines distinct levels of synchronization, likely used to control the frequency or scope of cache operations.

This class represents a synchronization task that manages database operations, including checking disk space, performing major or minor synchronization, and potentially switching the database to read-only mode if disk space is insufficient.
This class manages a pool of Serializer objects, responsible for their creation, pooling, and resetting to ensure efficient reuse of serialization resources.

This abstract class serves as a foundation for creating custom filters that can modify the serialization output of the Serializer. It allows for the registration of these custom filters within the system's configuration.
This interface defines a receiver that is part of a chain, allowing for the sequential processing of events and providing methods to manage the chain's structure.

This class acts as a filter for WSDL documents, augmenting the 'definitions' element with specific XML namespace declarations for 'tns' and 'soapenc' during SAX parsing, before passing the modified stream to an output handler. It specifically addresses a workaround for the Xalan XSLT processor.
This factory is responsible for creating and managing a chain of receivers, allowing for sequential processing of requests.

This class acts as a base implementation for a chain of receivers, allowing subclasses to selectively handle events while ensuring that all events are passed to the next receiver in the chain by default.
This class represents a detailed error encountered during resource operations, capable of storing a descriptive message and an optional underlying exception.

This class acts as a filter for an XML event stream, specifically designed to intercept and process XInclude elements. When an XInclude element is encountered, it attempts to embed the content of the referenced external resource at that position in the document, handling potential fallback mechanisms and errors during the inclusion process.

This class defines a collection of constants representing configuration options for XML and JSON serialization, controlling aspects like output formatting, namespace handling, and specific serialization behaviors.

This class is responsible for creating and managing a linked list of custom match listeners, often used for filtering during serialization processes. It is instantiated per serializer and configured via system properties or provided class names.
This class serializes XML nodes to a receiver, handling various node types, namespaces, and attributes, and is specifically designed for a native database backend.
Manages a pool of `Serializer` objects, providing a mechanism to borrow and return them for use within the application, optimizing resource utilization for XML serialization.

This class provides custom resolution logic for XSLT include and import directives, enabling the transformer to locate and process stylesheets from various sources, including internal resources tied to a specific collection.
This class implements an error listener for XML transformations that simply re-throws any exceptions encountered, serving as a mechanism to propagate errors.

This abstract class provides the core functionality for serializing XML documents or fragments into various output formats, including strings and SAX event streams, with extensive support for configuration options and XSL transformations.
This class manages a global memory pool for page caches, dynamically adjusting individual cache sizes based on available memory and cache load, and can shrink caches if they are underutilized.
This class manages a queue of system maintenance tasks, allowing them to be added and processed sequentially when the system is ready.
This class provides factory methods for serializing and deserializing Indexable objects to and from byte arrays, facilitating data storage and retrieval.
This enum defines the different modes for indexing data: storing new data, repairing existing data, or removing data.
This enum defines types for controlling whether collection and document attributes are preserved when making copies, with options for default behavior, no preservation, or explicit preservation.

This interface defines the contract for interacting with various database backends, providing fundamental operations for managing collections, documents, and their associated metadata, including indexing, storage, retrieval, and deletion.

This class provides a simple, growable list to store node identifiers along with their corresponding offsets within a text sequence. It facilitates adding new occurrences, retrieving nodes and offsets by position, checking for the existence of a node, and sorting the occurrences based on their offsets.
This class represents a custom exception that is thrown when an error occurs during database object management, such as creating or dropping collections or indexes.

This class provides utilities for rebuilding index files, specifically focusing on B+-tree based indexes by reconstructing them from their leaf pages. It also manages the lifecycle of the associated broker pool, including starting it up and shutting it down, and can be executed as a command-line utility to repair specified indexes.
This class aggregates and reports metrics for a B-Tree, tracking the counts of different page types (leaf, inner, data) and allowing for their printing or logging.

This class represents a log entry for the creation of a B-tree node, storing its status and page number information, and provides methods for redoing the creation, serialization, deserialization, and a string representation.
This class logs updates to a database page, capturing its state before and after the change to enable recovery and redo operations.
This interface defines a callback mechanism for B-Tree queries, allowing clients to receive index information and potentially terminate the enumeration process.
This class represents a loggable record for an update operation that modifies a value at a specific page and index, storing the new and old pointers associated with that value.
This class represents a custom exception specifically for B-tree operations, indicating an error during the management of the B-tree data structure.
This class defines primitive index query operations with various comparison operators and values, used for testing value matches.

This class represents a log entry for inserting a value into a B-tree, capturing details like the page number, index within the page, and the value itself, along with its corresponding pointer information.

This class logs changes related to setting a page link, capturing the current page number and the next page number for transactional purposes. It supports reading from and writing to a buffer, calculating log size, redoing operations, and providing a human-readable dump of the logged information.

This abstract class provides a base for loggable objects that interact with a native broker and manage a file identifier. It defines methods for reading and writing this identifier to and from byte buffers, and for determining the size of log entries.

This class manages metadata related to a data file, including its version, page structure, record counts, and free space management, and provides methods for reading and writing this metadata to and from storage.

This class represents a single page of data within a larger storage system, managing its header, offset, page number, and reference count. It provides functionality to read, write, clear, and compare page data, and to manage its lifecycle through reference counting.

This class manages the metadata for a page, including its status, the length of its data, a pointer to the next page, and the log sequence number of the last modification, and handles reading and writing this metadata to and from a byte array.

This class provides a foundational layer for managing data stored in fixed-size pages within a file, handling file operations, page allocation, and data retrieval for structures like B-trees. It acts as an abstract base class, requiring subclasses to define specific file and page header implementations.
This class holds information about a tree structure, specifically the identifier of the first page and the count of leaf pages.

Represents a node within a B+-tree, capable of storing keys and pointers to child nodes or data. It manages its own data persistence through an underlying Page object and supports operations like searching, inserting, removing, and splitting.

This class manages the header information for a B-tree file, including the root page identifier and the fixed length of keys stored within the tree. It handles reading and writing this header data to and from a byte buffer.
This class represents the header for a page within a B-tree data structure, storing information about the number of values and the identifier of its parent page.

This class implements a general-purpose B+-tree for storing binary keys, where the actual data values are stored separately and referenced by pointers. It provides core tree operations like adding, removing, and searching for values, as well as mechanisms for querying, rebuilding, and logging changes for recovery.
This class represents a loggable operation that records the setting of a parent page number for a given page within a transactional database system.
This class represents a loggable entry for the removal of a value from a data structure, storing the necessary information to redo and undo this operation.

This class represents an immutable sequence of bytes, serving as a fundamental data-holding object within the system. It provides methods for accessing its data, comparing it with other byte sequences, and determining common prefixes or suffixes.
This class records and tracks the history of queries, including their source, invocation count, execution time, and duration, and is designed to be used in a delayed execution context.
This class acts as a signal to control the continuation or termination of a process, allowing it to be stopped externally.
This class encapsulates information about a job, including its associated thread, action, start time, and a monitor, and provides functionality to stop the monitoring process.

This class monitors and manages actively running queries and jobs within a database instance, providing mechanisms to signal shutdown to running queries, track job execution, and terminate them if necessary.
This class defines a custom exception type used to signal errors originating from the BrokerPoolService.
This class represents the start of a transaction, providing methods to serialize and deserialize transaction start data.
This class represents a custom exception specifically for transactional errors, providing context and a mechanism to propagate issues related to transaction management within the system.
This class represents a transaction commit, holding transaction details and providing methods for logging its state.
This class represents a transaction abort operation, storing the transaction ID and providing methods for logging and state management.
This enum represents the possible states a transaction can be in, indicating its lifecycle from initiation to completion or termination.
This class encapsulates a lock resource and a corresponding action to release or close it, intended for managing the lifecycle of a lock.
This class acts as a wrapper around an existing transaction, enabling it to be reused as if it were a standard, single-use transaction.
This class represents a transaction, managing its state, acquired locks, and associated listeners, and provides methods to commit, abort, or close the transaction.
This interface defines a contract for objects that can be committed to finalize changes or aborted to discard them, acting as a transactional control mechanism.
This class maintains a count of operations within a transaction, primarily to detect uncommitted transactions during system shutdown.

Manages the lifecycle of transactions within the system, providing mechanisms to begin, commit, abort, and close them. It also handles system tasks and ensures thread-safe concurrent access through non-blocking, lock-free operations.
This class represents a checkpoint in a logging system, storing a transaction ID and its associated Log Sequence Number (LSN) along with a timestamp.
This interface defines a contract for objects that can be indexed. It specifies methods for serializing the object's value into a byte array for persistent storage and for retrieving its type.
This interface defines the contract for managing a collection of caches, including their registration, deregistration, size management, and overall monitoring.

This interface defines a contract for services that interact with a BrokerPool throughout its lifecycle, from initial configuration and preparation through various start-up and shut-down phases for system and multi-user modes.
This class provides an interface for accessing and managing journal recovery files, enabling operations such as setting recovery status, retrieving files, and switching between them.
This class is responsible for database recovery. It verifies the database's consistency upon startup and attempts to restore it from a journal log if inconsistencies are detected.
This class represents a reference to a specific node within a document, identified by its document ID and node ID.
This class represents a node that has been removed, storing its original node, its path, and its content.

This class acts as a delegate for processing nodes, specifically for indexing purposes. It manages the state required for indexing a node, updating its indices, and potentially storing it in the database.

This class acts as a callback for a B-tree, responsible for retrieving document data from a database based on a key and pointer, and then incorporating that document into a collection, with special handling for binary documents.
This enum defines the possible types of changes that can occur, specifically a push or a pop operation.
This class represents a traceable change to a subject, specifically used for logging or auditing alterations such as pushing or popping subjects.
This class provides low-level file-based XML database operations, managing collections, documents, and their associated indexes and metadata.
Represents a hierarchical path of qualified names, allowing for operations like appending, component addition, and matching against other paths, with an option to include descendants.
This class acts as a specific type of term matcher that verifies if an input character sequence exactly matches a stored expression.
This class provides a way to determine if a character sequence contains a specific expression.

This class implements a term matching strategy that verifies if a given character sequence starts with a predefined expression. It's designed for prefix-based filtering and matching operations within the system.
This class is responsible for checking if a given string ends with a specified expression, returning true if it does and false otherwise.
This class checks if a given text sequence matches a specific string expression, considering different truncation rules (left, right, both, or exact) using a provided collator for comparison.

This class processes stored document information from a database based on a given pointer, retrieving documents and their nodes and conditionally adding them to a result set based on context and ancestor relationships.
This class processes values during indexing by checking if their keys match a specified pattern, and if so, proceeds with indexing and key reuse.

This class acts as a callback mechanism to process index information and record document occurrences associated with specific values, ultimately building a map of values to their occurrences within a given context.

This class represents a key that combines a qualified name (QName) with an atomic value. It implements the Comparable interface to allow for ordering based on its QName and then its value, facilitating sorting and comparison operations.
This class represents a simple value, potentially within a collection, and handles its serialization and deserialization from byte arrays.
This class represents a simple prefix value, storing an integer collection ID and a type.

This class represents a qualified name (QName) value, storing its namespace URI, local name, and associated atomic value within a collection. It provides methods for serialization and deserialization from byte arrays.
This class represents a value associated with a qualified name (QName) and a prefix, likely used for managing symbol tables or namespaces within the system.
This class listens to the XML stream processing events, specifically managing the content of elements that are configured for indexing and storing attributes.
This code defines an enumeration that represents different types of indexes, each associated with a specific byte value.
This class represents a collection of pending changes to an index, keyed by a generic type K and storing a list of NodeIds for each key.
This class enables matching index entries against a regular expression, determining whether an entire entry or a part of it matches the specified pattern.
This class generates statistics about XML storage, specifically focusing on the status of database instances and their associated buffers, and outputs this information in an XML format.

This class provides a static method to compute and aggregate statistics related to various index types, such as DOM files, collection B-tree indexes, and native value indexes, based on provided configuration and a mutable map for storing the results.

This interface defines a contract for executing tasks synchronously during database startup, ensuring these tasks complete before the database is accessible to clients. While the execution blocks the startup process, any runtime exceptions are suppressed, and the startup proceeds. Implementations can optionally initiate asynchronous operations, but with limitations on accessing system resources.
This class aggregates and provides access to statistics for both index and data buffers within a database file, likely for performance monitoring or analysis.
This class manages a collection of database instances, providing methods to configure, retrieve, and stop them, ensuring proper shutdown and handling of concurrent access.
This class wraps a DBBroker to add tracing capabilities, logging the broker's reference count and call stack when tracing is activated.
This class is responsible for tracing the lease of a broker, primarily for debugging purposes, by keeping track of brokers that have been added and checking for timeouts.
This class represents a loggable operation for a split page in a DOM database, capable of recording, redoing, and undoing the changes associated with the split.

This class represents a position within a document, including the specific page, an offset on that page, and an identifier for a tuple. It also carries a flag indicating if this position refers to a link.
This class represents a loggable entry for adding a value, storing transaction details, page number, and the value itself, with functionality to redo, undo, and serialize this operation.

This class represents a log entry for a page removal operation in a database, storing information about the removed page, its previous and next links, and its old data content. It provides methods for serializing and deserializing this log entry, calculating its size, and performing redo and undo operations to manage the database state.
This class manages atomic operations on a DOM file, ensuring exclusive access by acquiring a lock before executing provided business logic and releasing the lock afterward.
This class acts as an iterator for traversing raw node data within a document, reading from data pages until the end of the document is reached, and providing the data for each node.
Provides an iterable and closable mechanism for traversing stored nodes, similar to a standard iterator but with resource management capabilities.

This class iterates over nodes in a DOM storage, ensuring data integrity by locking the DOM file during reads to prevent value changes. It supports navigating to the next node, retrieving its address, and repositioning the iterator.

This class represents a logged operation that updates a value within a database, storing both the new and old values along with transactional and positional information for recovery and auditing purposes.
This class provides utility methods for manipulating and querying status bits within a record identifier used in the dom.dbx persistent DOM store.
This class logs and replays operations related to writing overflow pages in a database, enabling recovery and rollback of these changes.
This class represents a logged operation for inserting a value into a specific page within the DOM database, designed to be used for transaction logging and recovery.
This class logs the removal of an empty page, storing its page number and its neighbors' page numbers, and provides functionality to redo or undo this removal operation.
This class represents a log entry for updating header information in a database, specifically managing page navigation pointers and their previous states.

This interface defines a mechanism for iterating through the raw nodes of a document, allowing repositioning to a specific node and sequential retrieval of node data, while also managing resource cleanup.

This class represents a log entry for creating a new page, storing information about the previous, current, and next pages, as well as a transaction identifier. It supports writing, reading, redoing, undoing, and dumping the state of this log entry.
This class logs changes related to updating a link, providing functionality to write, read, redo, undo, and dump the log entries.
This class represents a loggable operation for adding a link to a database, including methods for serialization, deserialization, redo, and undo operations within a transactional context.
This class represents a log entry for adding a value that has been moved, maintaining a backlink to its previous location.

This class represents a loggable operation for removing overflow data from a database, storing information about the page number, next page number, and the old data that was removed. It supports writing to and reading from byte buffers, calculating its log size, and performing redo and undo operations to manage the database state.
This class represents a log entry for removing a value from a database, storing information necessary to redo or undo the operation, including the original data and its location.
This class extends a base node path to track real node/element paths, not just QName paths, which is necessary for implementing more elaborate XPath expressions in configurations.
This class defines the discrete states that the system can be in throughout its lifecycle, from initial registration to shutting down.

This enum defines a set of distinct events that represent different stages or states within a system's lifecycle, such as configuration, preparation, entering and exiting various operational modes, and shutdown.

This class manages the lifecycle of various BrokerPool services, orchestrating their registration, configuration, and sequential startup and shutdown across different operational modes of the broker pool, from initial registration through to multi-user operation and eventual shutdown.

This class acts as a factory for creating different database broker implementations based on configuration. It manages the registration and retrieval of these brokers, ensuring that the appropriate database access logic is instantiated for a given application context.
This class manages a collection of startup triggers, acting as a unified service for their configuration and execution during system startup.
This interface defines a contract for observers that react to document loading and removal events, typically by updating or managing various types of indices.

This abstract class serves as a foundation for specific index implementations that manage structural information about elements within documents, enabling efficient searching and matching of elements based on their qualified names and types.
Specifies a range index on a node path, indexing node values according to a predefined type.

This class serves as a callback mechanism to log events related to system export operations, including the start of data collection, the initiation of document processing, and any errors encountered during the process.
This class acts as a callback handler for progress and status updates during consistency checks and system export operations, logging relevant information and tracking errors.
This class orchestrates a database consistency check, with options to create backups, generate zip files, and control incremental checking behavior.
This class acts as a global pool for compiled XQuery expressions, storing and retrieving them based on their source to optimize query execution by reusing already compiled queries.

This class listens to events during an XML document traversal, specifically tracking the depth and statistics of elements encountered. It maintains a stack to manage the state of nested elements and updates overall document statistics upon element completion.

This class handles the regeneration of index statistics for documents within a collection, specifically focusing on updating XML documents by retrieving, typing, and processing them based on a provided key and pointer. Errors encountered during this process are logged.
This class is responsible for updating and managing index statistics, including processing document data and flushing aggregated statistics.
Collects and manages statistics on element distribution within the database, storing this information in a graph structure that aids in query optimization.

This class represents the root node for serializing and deserializing node statistics, enabling data persistence and transmission, as well as generating SAX events for hierarchical data representation.

This class builds and maintains a graph representing the frequency and size distribution of elements and their paths within a document or database, enabling analysis of data structure. It can serialize and deserialize this graph to and from a byte channel.

This class collects and aggregates statistical information for a single node within a hierarchical data structure, tracking metrics like node count and maximum depth, and supporting operations for merging, serialization, and representation.

This class implements a blocking, thread-safe, in-memory buffer that couples producer and consumer threads. Producers write to the buffer, and consumers read from it. Producers block if the buffer is full, and consumers block if it is empty. It also supports signaling exceptions during closure to unblock waiting threads.
This class provides a way to read data from an underlying input stream using a variable-byte encoding scheme, allowing for efficient storage and retrieval of data.
This class provides a mechanism to read variable-length encoded data from a byte array.
This class acts as an adapter, allowing an output stream to interact with a blocking input stream by providing standard output stream operations.

This abstract class provides a base implementation for reading various data types (bytes, shorts, ints, longs, strings) and performing stream operations like skipping and copying from a variable-byte encoded input stream.

This class provides an output stream that writes data using a variable-byte encoding scheme, optimizing storage for integer types based on their magnitude. It allows for writing individual bytes, byte arrays, shorts, integers, longs, and strings, as well as providing methods to manage and retrieve the buffered data.

This interface defines methods for reading data that is encoded using a variable byte format, suitable for efficient storage of smaller values. It provides operations to read individual bytes, shorts, integers, longs, and strings, as well as methods for skipping or copying data to an output stream.

This abstract class defines specifications for range indexes, mapping between internal index types and external XPath types, and providing utility methods for checking index properties like range, qualified name, or value/mixed presence.
This class acts as a callback mechanism for writing data into a ZIP archive, managing the creation and closing of individual entries within the archive.
This class handles the process of backing up data, creating timestamped zip archives in a specified destination directory.
This class represents a value that can be either an element or an attribute, identified by a collection ID and type.
This interface defines a contract for objects that can receive and process key-value information. Implementations are expected to handle the storage or further processing of this data.
This class represents a loggable entry for an overflow page, handling the serialization, deserialization, and re-application of page data and metadata within a database transaction.
This class represents a loggable entry for modifications to an overflow page within a B-File system, specifically tracking changes related to page numbers, lengths, and chain linkage.

This class represents a block of free space within a data page, storing its page number and the amount of available space. It is used to manage and track free space, likely as part of a larger data management or storage system.
This class represents a unique identifier for a document within a collection, providing methods to construct and extract its components.
Represents a key for identifying and accessing collections, with constants defining offsets and lengths for its internal structure.

This class manages the storage and retrieval of collections and documents, including the allocation and deallocation of their unique identifiers. It also provides mechanisms for flushing cached data to persistent storage.
This class represents a log entry for an overflow data removal operation within a database system, encapsulating the necessary information to replay, reverse, or inspect such an operation.
This class collects pointers to values during a tree traversal, storing them for later processing.
Manages a list of available data pages within a B-tree file, facilitating efficient allocation and deallocation of storage space.
This class represents and manages the header information for a page within a B-tree file structure, including details about record counts, data length, and chain linkages.
This abstract class represents a data page within a data storage system, handling data manipulation, reference counting for caching, and synchronization with persistent storage.

This class acts as an adapter, processing data from a B-tree structure and relaying it to a specific file callback mechanism. It intercepts index information, potentially filtering or transforming it before passing it on.
