This code defines a domain-specific language (DSL) for describing and executing sequences of database transaction operations. It uses a type-safe builder pattern to construct schedules, ensuring that operations receive the correct input types based on previous operations' outputs, and allows for the concurrent execution of two independent transaction branches.

This abstract class provides a foundation for testing XQuery compilation, offering utility methods to compile and execute XQuery strings against an eXist-db instance. It is designed to facilitate the creation of specific test suites by handling the common setup and execution logic.
This class provides a JUnit rule for managing an embedded eXist-db database instance during integration tests, handling its startup, shutdown, and configuration.

This class acts as a Hamcrest matcher for comparing XML content represented as strings. It provides static factory methods to create matchers for both identical and similar XML comparisons, and its core functionality lies in verifying if an input XML string conforms to a specified expected XML structure and content.

This class provides a suite of assertion methods specifically designed for testing XQuery compilation, execution, and error handling, facilitating easier validation of XQuery-related operations within a test environment.

This class defines a collection of constant values, primarily consisting of URIs and strings that represent paths and names used for testing purposes within the system. It includes pre-encoded and decoded versions of special characters and standard file/collection names.
This class provides functionality to serialize and deserialize sequences and items to and from XML representations, and to convert streamed XML data into DOM Nodes.
Represents a single validation issue encountered during processing, storing details such as its type, location, message, and frequency.
This class facilitates the redirection of external resource references for applications, particularly when used with `javax.xml.validation.Validator`.

This class acts as a resolver for XML entities and URIs, leveraging a connection pool to interact with an eXist-DB database. It provides functionality to translate public and system identifiers, as well as URI references, into input sources or transform sources, enabling the integration of external XML resources and data within the application.
This class provides a mechanism to redirect references to external resources by allowing applications to supply their own input streams or string data.

This class resolves XML external entities by first attempting to use a provided URI and then falling back to an expanded system identifier if necessary, managing the resolution process across multiple attempts.
This class is responsible for resolving XML resources by querying a database using either a namespace or a public identifier, and then returning an XML input source for the found resource.

This class is designed to process an XML document, specifically identifying and storing the namespace URI of the document's root element. It achieves this by leveraging the SAX (Simple API for XML) parsing mechanism.
This class encapsulates information about a class, including its descriptive name, its required version, and a mechanism (a fully qualified function name) to retrieve its actual runtime version.

This class provides functionality to check for the presence and compatibility of required XML processing libraries, including parsers, transformers, and resolvers, ensuring the system has the necessary components for XML operations.
This class aggregates and reports all validation information, including errors and warnings encountered during a process, and tracks the duration of that process.
This class provides a way to uniquely identify and compare grammar configurations based on their type and target namespace, enabling efficient management within a cache.

This class implements a grammar cache using the Caffeine library to store and retrieve XML grammars, optimizing performance by reducing repeated parsing. It provides methods to cache, retrieve, clear, and manage the state (locked/unlocked) of the grammar pool.

This class validates XML documents against various grammars, including DTDs and Schemas (XSD), using different validation libraries like Jing and Xerces. It supports validation against system catalogs and user-specified grammars, returning detailed validation reports.
This class is responsible for serializing a node to an output stream, handling potential IO exceptions during the process and ensuring the stream is properly managed.
This class is responsible for serializing a node value into an output stream using a specified serializer and output properties.
This class serializes a node into an input stream, allowing it to be read byte by byte or in chunks.
This class serves as a utility for accessing and executing predefined XQuery resources stored within the application, primarily for database interaction related to schema and catalog lookups.

This class represents a conditional modification that evaluates an XQuery. If the query returns true, it applies a list of other modifications; otherwise, it does nothing. It aggregates multiple modifications to be applied conditionally.

This class represents an XUpdate rename operation, allowing for the renaming of selected nodes within XML documents. It handles the necessary database interactions, document management, and permission checks to perform these modifications.
This class implements the XUpdate update modification, handling the processing of transactions to update or create nodes within documents, managing permissions, locking, and notifications.
This class represents an XUpdate modification to insert nodes either before or after a specified node within an XML document.
This class represents an operation to append child nodes to selected elements within XML documents, with the capability to overwrite existing attributes.

This is an abstract base class defining the fundamental operations and state for modifications to XML documents within the XUpdate framework, including processing, selection, locking, and trigger management.
This class processes an XUpdate XML request, parsing it using SAX and compiling it into a series of modifications that can be applied to a document.
This class implements the xupdate:replace extension for the XUpdate standard, providing functionality to replace entire nodes, including their content, within an XML document.

This class implements an XUpdate remove operation, responsible for processing transactions that involve removing nodes from documents within a specified document set based on a select statement and associated variables.

This interface defines a contract for interacting with a database, providing access to its various managers, brokers, and configuration, as well as methods for authentication, shutdown, and managing triggers and observers.
This class defines an enumeration to categorize the purpose of a query, differentiating between setup, pre-installation, post-installation, and undeployment operations.
This class represents a request for user permissions, including the user's credentials, an optional group, and either an integer or string representation of the permissions.

This class is responsible for updating a repository XML file during its processing, with a specific focus on removing sensitive information like default passwords before the file is finalized or uploaded.
This class handles the installation, deployment, and uninstallation of software packages within the database, including managing dependencies and performing necessary setup and cleanup operations.
This class encapsulates and manages different versioning schemes, including minimum, maximum, and semantic versions, providing access to these version representations.
This class defines an interface for loading expath packages, specifying how to locate a package by name and version, and includes an inner class to represent different package version schemes.
This class initiates the automatic deployment of application packages by scanning a designated directory for `.xar` files and installing any applications not already present in the database.
This class is responsible for managing and constructing the classpath for expath modules that include JAR files, specifically within the context of eXist-db's startup process.
This class acts as a URI resolver specifically designed to locate and retrieve XSLT modules packaged within EXPath packages from an eXist repository.
This class handles the parsing and installation of `exist.xml` descriptors within an EXPath package, facilitating the management and setup of these packages in a repository.
This class provides utility methods for creating compressed backups of the expath file system repository and restoring the repository from a compressed archive.
This enum defines a set of possible actions that can be performed, specifically installation and uninstallation.
This class represents a notification containing an action and a package URI.

This class acts as a repository for EXPath packages, enabling the resolution and loading of Java, XQuery, and XSLT modules and providing notifications for repository actions like installation and uninstallation.
This class extends PackageInfo to provide eXist-specific package information, managing resources like JARs, Java functions, and XQuery files associated with a package.

This interface defines a factory for creating and managing unique identifiers (NodeIds) for nodes within a system, supporting various initialization methods, deserialization from different data formats, and retrieval of specific node types like the document root.

This interface defines the contract for internal identifiers of nodes within eXist, enabling their ordering and relationship determination within a document structure, and supporting their storage and retrieval.
This class provides a base implementation for representing and encoding node identifiers using a variable-length, prefix-free binary encoding scheme suitable for dynamic level numbers.
This class represents a hierarchical node identifier (DLN) that supports efficient insertion of new nodes between existing ones by utilizing sublevel identifiers.

This class acts as a factory for creating and managing DLN-based node identifiers, providing methods to create them from various sources like integers, streams, byte arrays, and strings, as well as a dedicated identifier for document nodes.
This class manages a collection of Java Archive (JAR) files intended for use with Web Start, providing mechanisms to locate, retrieve, and determine the last modification time of these JARs.

This servlet is responsible for serving JNLP files, JAR archives, and image files to facilitate Java Web Start application deployment and execution. It initializes by locating necessary libraries and handles incoming HTTP GET requests to deliver these resources.
This class is responsible for generating and serving resources related to Java Web Start applications, including the JNLP configuration file, JAR archives, and image assets.
This class resolves a filename to its latest version if it contains a '%latest%' token, otherwise it returns the filename as is.

This interface defines the contract for managing the lifecycle of database operations, including starting and stopping transactions and synchronizing data. It is deprecated in favor of a more granular event-driven approach.
This interface defines a contract for accessing common properties of any generic database resource, including its unique identifier and associated permissions.
This class provides an input stream for reading document data from a remote database via XML-RPC, allowing the document content to be processed as a stream of bytes.
This class is responsible for downloading documents from a remote XML database via XMLRPC and writing the document's content into an output stream, handling large documents by reading them in chunks.
This class wraps an `XmlrpcUpload` instance into a `Runnable` for execution within an `XmlrpcOutputStream`, facilitating asynchronous data uploads.
This class provides an output stream that writes data to a remote database via XML-RPC, buffering output before sending.
This class wraps the XmlrpcDownload functionality into a Runnable, allowing for asynchronous execution of downloading a resource from a URL and writing it to a provided output stream.
This class handles uploading documents to a remote eXist-db server using XML-RPC, supporting both XML and binary content, and enabling large file uploads through chunking.

This class provides a wrapper and convenience methods for working with xmldb URLs, which are used to represent resource locations in an XML database, offering functionalities like parsing and extracting components of these URLs.
This class acts as a factory for creating custom stream handlers specifically for the 'xmldb' protocol, allowing for unique ways to handle data streams within the system.
This class manages the translation of a URL object into a resource stream, simulating URL connection behavior.
Manages the translation of a URL object into a resource stream, providing a connection to embedded resources.
This class handles connections for the 'xmldb:' protocol, enabling interaction with XML databases through custom URL schemes.
This enum defines two distinct modes for handling data streams: either by keeping the data in memory or by storing it on disk to manage memory usage.
Provides an InputStream interface to read document content from an embedded database, lazily initializing the underlying stream and ensuring proper resource management.

This class acts as an in-memory buffer for data before it is streamed to an XML database. It intercepts standard output stream operations and redirects them to an internal byte array, providing methods to eventually send this buffered data to a specified XML database URL.
This class acts as an output stream that writes data directly to a local embedded database, managing the underlying stream operations and ensuring the stream is properly closed and flushed.
This class provides a static method to create an InputStream for accessing document or binary resources from a database via a given URL, ensuring the URL does not point to a collection.

This class is responsible for registering the eXist-db URL stream handler factory, ensuring that custom protocol handlers for eXist can be utilized by the Java runtime. It acts as a startup trigger, executing once to set up this crucial component for handling custom data streams within the application.
This interface defines a contract for objects that listen for and process responses to commands, enabling asynchronous command execution and continuation.

This interface defines the contract for representing various types of breakpoints, including line, call, return, exception, conditional, and watch breakpoints, along with their properties and state management. It also provides methods for XML serialization, synchronization of changes, and removal.
This interface defines a contract for objects that represent a source code location, providing methods to retrieve its file URI and starting line and column numbers.
This interface defines the contract for objects that represent variables, providing methods to retrieve their name, value, and type.
This class represents a custom exception that is thrown when a timeout occurs during an operation.
This interface defines the contract for objects that represent a response, providing methods to access transaction identifiers, attributes, text content, and elements by name.

This interface defines the contract for interacting with a debugging session, enabling operations such as initializing the session, controlling execution flow (running, stepping, stopping), retrieving debugging information (source, variables, stack frames), and evaluating expressions.
This interface defines the contract for interacting with a debugging session, allowing control over script execution, inspection of program state, and management of breakpoints.
This class provides an iterator for a sorted set of nodes, allowing traversal and access to individual items and node proxies.

This class represents an item within an iterator, holding a proxy to a node and an optional string value. It defines how these items are compared and checked for equality, ensuring correct ordering and uniqueness within the iteration process.
This class represents a collection of nodes that are maintained in a sorted order based on a specified expression.
Provides functionality to add, clear, and manage documents within a set, with options for duplicate checking and adding entire collections or other document sets.

This class represents a segment of data or a range within a larger structure, defined by a starting position and a length. It provides methods to retrieve these values and to determine if two such segments overlap.

This class tracks occurrences of matching terms within text nodes, storing information about the node, the matched term, its frequency, and its specific positions (offsets and lengths). It supports operations for combining, filtering, and expanding these matches, as well as checking for overlaps and containment.
This interface defines a contract for objects that visit stored nodes, allowing them to be notified of the current node during traversal and decide whether to continue the visit.
This class represents an iterator for an empty set of nodes, providing methods to indicate the absence of elements and to signal errors when operations like 'next' or 'remove' are attempted.
This class implements an iterator that always indicates an empty collection and throws an exception if modification is attempted.

This class represents an empty set of nodes, providing no-operation implementations for methods that would typically modify or query a node set, and always returning empty iterators or default values.

This class represents an empty set of documents, providing default behavior for operations that would otherwise require accessing actual document data. All operations on this empty set consistently return empty results or false, reflecting its null state.

This class represents a persistent document in a database, capable of storing XML, binary files, or XQuery source code. It manages document metadata, permissions, and relationships with its containing collection.
This class represents and manages a CDATA section within an XML document, handling its serialization and deserialization, and providing methods for text manipulation.
This class represents and persists a processing instruction node within a Document Object Model (DOM) structure, handling its target and data content.
This class represents a node that has a qualified name (QName), serving as a base for elements or attributes within a structured data context.

This class provides a collection of static utility methods for performing various operations on sets of nodes, including selecting parent-child relationships, ancestor-descendant relationships, siblings, preceding/following nodes, and attributes, as well as copying nodes.
This interface defines the contract for nodes that are stored, providing methods for serialization, managing ownership by a document, and handling node lifecycle and modification status.
This class acts as a mutable container for a reference to an `IStoredNode`, allowing the node to be passed and modified by reference within the system.

Represents a collection of documents, providing methods to access, manipulate, and compare document sets, including operations like intersection, containment checks, locking, and conversion to other data structures.

This interface extends the standard Java Iterator to provide additional capabilities for iterating over a set of nodes, specifically allowing a look-ahead inspection of the current node and the ability to reposition the iterator to a specific node.

This class traverses a node structure, identifying and storing the last attribute node encountered and the first child node that belongs to the current element. It stops traversing down a branch if a child node belonging to the current element is found.

This class represents an XML element within a document, managing its attributes, child nodes, and namespace declarations. It provides methods for serialization, deserialization, manipulation of its content (adding, removing, replacing children and attributes), and querying its properties.

This class represents a placeholder for a set of relevant nodes, enabling deferred resolution of XPath expressions to avoid inefficiently retrieving all descendant nodes. It primarily provides functionality to find the first matching descendant based on specific criteria.
This class represents an item within a context, holding a reference to a node and potentially linking to the next item in a direct sequence.

This class provides an in-order traversal of a binary tree, allowing iteration over its nodes and items. It supports checking for the next element, retrieving the next node or item, and peeking at the next node without removal, but does not support removing elements.
This class represents a node within a binary tree, storing data, parent, and child references, along with height information to manage tree structure and balance.

This class implements a set of nodes using a self-balancing binary search tree (AVL tree) to efficiently store and manage nodes while maintaining order and facilitating quick lookups, additions, and deletions.
This enum defines different types of symbols, each associated with a unique byte identifier.
This class manages a collection of symbols, allowing them to be looked up by either their integer identifier or their string name, and provides methods for writing these symbols to an output stream.

This class manages a collection of local names for symbols, distinguishing between element and attribute names by using a prefix for attribute names in persistent storage while omitting it for in-memory storage.

This class maintains a global symbol table that maps namespace URIs and node names to unique numeric IDs, which are used internally by the database to represent these entities. It persists this mapping to a file and manages its loading and saving.

Represents a collection of nodes within a document structure, supporting operations for navigation, manipulation, and set-based comparisons such as intersection, union, and difference. It facilitates querying and processing of XML or similar hierarchical data by providing methods to access, filter, and relate nodes based on their relationships (parent, child, ancestor, descendant) and document origins.
This class wraps a document with a lock, ensuring the lock is released when the document is no longer needed through automatic resource management.

This class acts as a temporary cache for Qualified Name (QName) objects, aiming to reduce repeated memory allocations by storing and reusing existing QNames. If the cache reaches its capacity, it is cleared to make space.
This class provides an iterator for a batch of documents, allowing sequential access to individual documents and preventing modifications to the batch during iteration.

This class acts as an iterator for a collection of nodes, providing methods to check for more elements, retrieve the next element, skip elements, and view the next element without advancing the iterator. It also explicitly disallows removal of elements.
This class manages a collection of nodes and their associated documents, providing efficient storage and retrieval operations, with optional sorting and duplicate removal.

This abstract class represents a node in a document object model (DOM) with support for expressions and transaction-based operations, although many of its DOM manipulation methods are explicitly unsupported.

This class serves as the base for all nodes that are stored persistently in a database, providing fundamental properties and behaviors for such nodes, including identification, ownership, and serialization mechanisms.
This interface defines the contract for objects that can be visited by a NodeVisitor. It enables a traversal mechanism where a visitor can perform an operation on each element of a node structure.
This class is responsible for handling the creation of XML documents and document types, as well as querying the availability of specific XML features.

This iterator provides a way to traverse a single node, offering methods to check for its existence, retrieve it, and manage its position, while also indicating that removal operations are not supported.
This class represents and manages a comment node within a Document Object Model (DOM), providing functionality for its serialization and deserialization.

This class represents and manipulates text nodes within a document, handling serialization, deserialization, and basic text operations. It extends abstract character data and implements the Text interface, suggesting it's part of a Document Object Model (DOM) implementation for handling text content.
This class represents a persistent binary document, storing its content as binary data and providing an interface consistent with other document types.
Manages a set of documents and their associated collections, providing methods for adding, retrieving, and comparing document sets.

This abstract class provides a base implementation for character data manipulation within an XML structure, offering methods to append, delete, insert, replace, and extract string data, while also managing the underlying XML string buffer and resource release.
This class provides an iterator for traversing a set of document nodes and yielding collections derived from them.

This abstract class defines the core behavior for collections of nodes, acting as a specialized sequence that can be iterated over, modified, and used in various node-related operations like parent-child and ancestor-descendant relationships, set operations (union, intersection, difference), and attribute selection.
This class represents and provides functionality to read and write an XML declaration, which includes version, encoding, and standalone attributes.

This method checks if a given node or its descendants exist within a specified set, optionally including the ancestor node itself, operating within the context of a document and allowing for copying matching nodes.

This class represents an attribute within an XML document, holding its name, namespace information, type, and value, and providing methods for serialization, deserialization, and manipulation of attribute data.
This class provides an iterator for traversing a sequence of documents or document parts, allowing for sequential access and retrieval of the next available document.
This class provides an iterator that wraps another iterator, allowing iteration over a collection of collections.

This class manages a collection of node proxies, providing functionality to add, retrieve, check for existence, sort, and identify relationships (parent-child, descendant) with other nodes. It also handles duplicate removal and determines index types based on its contents.
This class iterates over a collection of data parts, providing sequential access to nodes and items within those parts.

This class provides an efficient array-based implementation for managing sets of nodes and documents, with features for maintaining order and handling duplicates. It allows for unordered storage during initial population and offers methods to sort and de-duplicate the set before iteration or specific query operations.
Represents a document type, storing its name, public ID, and system ID, and providing access to its entities and notations.

This class holds and manages metadata associated with a document, including timestamps, MIME type, page count, and lock information. It is deprecated and its functionality is being migrated to `DocumentImpl`.

This enum defines different types of locks that can be applied, including no lock, a write lock, and a state where the lock type is not set. It also provides functionality to retrieve the byte representation of each lock type and to find a lock type based on its byte value.
This code defines an enumeration for lock depths, providing a byte representation for each depth level and a method to retrieve an enum value from its byte representation.
This enumeration defines different types of lock scopes (NONE, EXCLUSIVE, SHARED, NOT_SET) and provides functionality to convert byte values to their corresponding enum representations.
Defines a set of enumerated resource types, each associated with a specific byte value, and provides functionality to retrieve a ResourceType based on its byte representation.

This class represents the details of a WebDAV lock, including its type, depth, scope, owner, timeout, and a unique opaque token. It provides functionality to generate and serialize lock token information.

This class provides a collection of static utility methods for processing and manipulating XML and related string data, including serialization, encoding/decoding of attribute markup, file reading, and value parsing.

This abstract class provides a base implementation for managing a collection of nodes, focusing on efficient storage and retrieval, particularly for array-like structures, and offers functionality for sorting, merging duplicates, and managing state changes.
This interface defines a handle to a document node, providing methods to set and retrieve its unique identifier and internal storage address within the database.
Manages a collection of in-scope XML namespaces using a reference counting mechanism for efficient access and management.
This class implements a StAX XMLStreamReader that operates on an in-memory DOM representation of an XML document, providing an alternative to reading from persistent storage.
This class acts as a SAX receiver, transforming XML events into an in-memory Document Object Model (DOM) tree.

This class represents an in-memory XML document, storing its nodes and associated data in arrays for efficient access and manipulation. It supports operations like adding nodes, attributes, and namespaces, as well as querying and serializing document fragments, with the ability to handle references to external nodes.
This class represents a CDATA section within an XML document, providing methods for accessing and manipulating its text content.
This class represents a processing instruction node within a document, allowing for the storage and retrieval of processing instruction data, as well as its conversion to an atomic string value.
Represents a node in a document that refers to another node, providing access to its properties and enabling attribute and child selection based on node tests.

This class represents an in-memory collection of nodes, providing methods to navigate and filter these nodes based on various relationships like children, descendants, ancestors, and siblings, as well as attribute and self-axis traversals.
This class builds an in-memory representation of an XML DOM document, handling the creation and organization of elements, text, comments, attributes, and other XML nodes.

This class represents an element within an XML document, handling its tag name, attributes, and child nodes, and supporting operations for querying and manipulating these aspects, including XPath-based selections.
This class is an iterator designed to traverse a sequence containing a single node, providing methods to check for the next element, retrieve the current element, and manage skipping elements.

Represents an abstract node within a document, providing core functionality for node manipulation, value retrieval, and document traversal, while also supporting XPath-related operations and serialization.
This class implements the DOMImplementation interface, providing methods to create new XML documents, document type definitions, and to query feature support.
This class represents an XML comment node within a document, providing methods to access its string value and type, and encapsulating its data as an atomic string.
This class represents a text node within a document, providing functionality to manipulate and retrieve its text content, including splitting and replacing the entire text.
This class is an adapter that modifies the behavior of a SAX adapter to always allow appending to it by disabling the start and end document events.
This class represents a dynamically constructed namespace node, used to track namespace declarations within elements, and it can be treated as a standard attribute.

This class acts as an adapter to build an in-memory document object model (DOM) from a SAX event stream, managing namespace declarations and handling character data, comments, and processing instructions.
Represents a lightweight fragment of a document, capable of holding a collection of nodes that can be inserted into a parent document.
This class provides foundational operations for managing character data within a document, including methods for retrieving, modifying, and selecting character-based information.

Represents an attribute within a document, providing methods to access and manipulate its name, value, type, and relationship to its owner element and parent node, while also supporting XPath-based node selections.
This class facilitates the efficient persistence of in-memory document fragments by directly writing them to a temporary database document, bypassing slower serialization methods.
This class provides a map-like data structure that maintains both key-value associations and an ordered list of keys, allowing for retrieval of values by key or by their position in the order.
This class manages a collection of named nodes, supporting retrieval, addition, and removal of nodes by name or namespace, and provides indexed access to the nodes.
This interface defines a contract for objects representing nodes within the eXist database, supporting both persistent and in-memory document structures.
This class provides a custom comparison logic for `QName` objects, ensuring that their `nameType`, namespace URI, and local name are considered during comparison.
Represents a generic node within the eXist database, supporting both persistent and in-memory documents and implementing standard DOM Node functionalities.
This interface defines a partial qualified name, serving as a marker for elements that represent an incomplete version of a fully qualified name.
This class represents a wildcard qualified name, providing a singleton instance for this specific type of name.
This class represents a qualified name (QName) where the namespace URI is treated as a wildcard, allowing for broader matching in certain contexts.

This class represents a qualified name where the local part is a wildcard, allowing for matching any local name within a specific namespace. It provides methods to construct such names and parse them from a given prefix using a provided context for namespace resolution.
This class defines a set of enumerated constants representing different validation states for a particular type of data, each with an associated byte value.
This class represents an exception that is thrown when a qualified name (QName) is invalid, carrying information about the nature of the invalidity.

This class represents a qualified name (QName), which is a combination of a local name, a namespace URI, and an optional prefix, enabling unique identification of elements and attributes within XML documents or similar structured data formats.
Manages a collection of Node objects, providing methods to add nodes and retrieve them by their position.
Provides utility methods for processing and formatting stack traces, allowing for extraction of specific portions and their conversion into human-readable string representations.
This class provides an implementation for a streamable MD2 digest, allowing for the incremental update and retrieval of a cryptographic hash.
This class acts as a wrapper around an existing output stream, calculating a cryptographic digest of all data written through it.
Represents a message digest, storing its type and byte value, and providing methods to access and represent this data.
This class provides a streamable interface for calculating a 160-bit Blake2b cryptographic digest, allowing data to be processed in chunks.
This class implements a streamable digest for the RIPEMD256 hashing algorithm, allowing for incremental updates and retrieval of the message digest.
This class implements a streamable digest for the Blake2b 512-bit hashing algorithm, allowing data to be processed in chunks for generating a message digest.

This class provides an implementation of the MD4 message digest algorithm that can be updated incrementally with streams of data, allowing for the calculation of a cryptographic hash over potentially large inputs without loading the entire input into memory at once. It supports updating the digest with individual bytes or byte arrays, copying the digest's current state, and resetting it for new calculations.

This class extends an input stream to compute a digest (like a checksum or hash) of the data as it is read. It wraps an existing input stream and intercepts read operations to update the digest calculation, providing the computed digest upon request.
This class implements a streamable digest for SHA-256, allowing incremental updates and retrieval of the message digest.
This class implements a streamable message digest using the MD5 algorithm, allowing data to be processed in chunks for calculating a hash.
This enum defines the types of message digests supported, mapping each type to its unique identifier, bit length, and a factory for creating digest instances.

This class implements a streamable SHA-1 cryptographic digest, allowing for incremental updates and retrieval of the message digest. It also supports creating copies of its internal state and resetting for new calculations.
This class provides a streamable interface for computing a 256-bit Blake2b cryptographic hash, allowing data to be processed in chunks.
This class implements the RIPEMD160 cryptographic hash function in a way that allows for incremental updates and copying of the digest state.
This interface defines the contract for objects that can compute a message digest from a stream of data, allowing for incremental updates and retrieval of the digest in various forms.
This class provides a streamable implementation for SHA-512 cryptographic hashing, allowing data to be processed in chunks for calculating a message digest.
Provides a thread-local storage for a pool of two-dimensional byte arrays.
Manages a pool of reusable byte arrays to optimize memory usage during document parsing, specifically for small byte chunks generated from DOM nodes.

This class provides various overloaded methods to sort arrays and lists of different types (comparable objects, longs, and NodeProxy objects) using a heap sort algorithm. It includes overloaded 'sort' methods that can take a Comparator or an auxiliary array for sorting, and internal 'fixHeap' methods to maintain the heap property during the sorting process.
This interface defines operations for managing and manipulating sequences of bytes, including setting the length, copying data to various destinations, and appending new bytes or byte arrays.
This class acts as a filter to identify files that are specifically of the 'application/xquery' media type and are not XML files.
This class tracks and reports progress, typically for long-running operations, by managing a current value against a maximum and notifying observers when a significant change occurs.
This class provides a standard way to create threads with a consistent naming convention, which can include an instance identifier and a base name for clarity.
This class manages the configuration for a single instance of the system, including locating configuration files and determining the web application home directory.

This class provides functionality to recursively scan XML database collections for resources matching a specified pattern. It supports two overloaded methods: one that returns a new array of matching resources and another that adds matching resources to an existing list.

This class provides an efficient, immutable view of a character array, allowing operations like length retrieval, character access, and substring extraction without creating new arrays, thus optimizing memory usage and performance by avoiding unnecessary data copying.
This class tracks the occurrences of a specific atomic value and the set of documents in which it appears, facilitating aggregation and comparison of these counts.

This abstract class represents a recorded change in the state of an object, along with information about the change itself, the state before the change, and the thread that performed the change. It provides a mechanism to trace and understand how the state evolved over time.
This class defines a custom exception to signal issues related to locking mechanisms within the application.

This class represents a specific type of exception that is thrown when a deadlock occurs, indicating a situation where two or more processes are unable to proceed because each is waiting for the other to release a resource.
Provides an input source for the system, allowing data to be read as either a string or a byte array.

This class provides utility methods to configure HttpsURLConnection for environments where SSL certificate validation or hostname verification needs to be bypassed, typically for development or testing purposes.

This class facilitates the recursive copying of a directory and its contents from a source path to a destination path. It handles the creation of directories and the copying of files while preserving the directory structure.
This class is responsible for recursively deleting a directory and its contents during a file system traversal.
This class traverses a file system and calculates the total size of all files visited.
Provides utility methods for performing various file and directory operations, including conversion, copying, deletion, size calculation, and path manipulation.
This class represents a node in a doubly linked list, storing a long value and references to the next and previous nodes.

This interface defines a stream reader for embedded XML content, providing methods to navigate and extract data from XML nodes. It supports repositioning the stream to a specific node, retrieving the current node and its predecessor, filtering nodes based on a custom criteria, and obtaining the node's type and text value.
This class represents a source of resources that can be loaded using the current context's class loader, handling resource names as paths within the classpath.

This class acts as a factory for creating `Source` objects, which represent various types of resources, by abstracting the logic for retrieving them from different locations like the classpath, database, or filesystem.
This class represents a source of binary data, providing methods to access its content as a byte array, input stream, or string, and includes functionality to check encoding.

This abstract class provides a base implementation for sources, handling key management and offering utility methods for encoding detection, module identification, and generating descriptive string representations.
This class represents a source of data read from the file system, providing access to file content, encoding, and metadata.
This enum defines a set of distinct states indicating whether something is valid or invalid.

This interface defines a contract for accessing data from various sources, enabling operations like reading content, retrieving paths, and identifying source types, primarily intended for loading XQuery scripts and modules.
This class serves as an abstraction for reading binary data stored in a database, providing access to the content, metadata, and permissions associated with the stored document.
This class provides a mechanism to read data from a specified URL, handling aspects like content retrieval, encoding, and validation for both local file paths and remote resources.
This class represents a source of data encapsulated within a single string, providing access to its content and type.

This interface defines the contract for atomic database transactions, providing methods to commit, abort, and close the transaction. It ensures that all operations within a transaction are treated as a single, indivisible unit, either succeeding entirely or failing entirely, thereby maintaining data consistency and integrity. The `close` method also handles automatic rollback if the transaction isn't explicitly committed.
This interface defines a contract for objects that listen for and process incoming events of a generic type `T`.

This interface defines a contract for accessing and describing backup content, including its structure, properties, and associated metadata. It allows for navigation through hierarchical backup structures and retrieval of specific backup components.
This class provides a graphical user interface for displaying and updating the status of a backup operation, showing the current collection and file being backed up, along with a progress bar.

This abstract class defines the common interface and fields for backup descriptors, including methods for retrieving the backup date and number of files, and for parsing XML data. It serves as a base for specific backup descriptor implementations.
This class represents a backup descriptor for a zip archive, allowing access to its contents as backup descriptors and input sources.

This class provides a graphical user interface for exporting data, allowing users to configure export settings, select a database, specify an output directory, and initiate the export process. It also includes functionalities for displaying messages, managing log files, and handling user interactions through buttons and menu items.
This class acts as a callback handler to report the status of a system export process, including the start of collection, progress on individual documents, and any errors encountered.
This class provides a callback mechanism to track the progress and report errors during a consistency check operation.

This class serves as the main entry point for exporting database contents. It parses command-line arguments to control export behavior, such as enabling/disabling checks, specifying output formats (directory or zip), and configuring database access. It orchestrates the database startup and initiates the export process based on the provided arguments.

This interface defines a callback mechanism for receiving progress updates and error notifications during document and collection processing. It allows external systems to monitor and react to the lifecycle of these operations.

This class handles the restoration of data from a backup file, including user authentication, potential credential updates, and the parsing of XML backup descriptors to import data, with progress reporting via a listener.
This class represents a deferred permission for an entry that is skipped during a restore process, effectively meaning no action is taken when its permissions are applied.
This class represents a detailed description of an application, including its file path, name, and semantic version.

This class provides utility methods for comparing applications found in a backup with those already installed in a package repository, aiding in the restore process by identifying outdated or superseded applications.

This class handles the deferred application of permission changes to a specific database resource, ensuring that ownership and access controls are updated correctly, even if the initial application fails.
This class represents a deferred permission that holds information about a target resource, its owner and group, and a list of Access Control Entries (ACEs) that will be applied at a later time.
This class handles the parsing of __contents__.xml files during the restoration process of a database backup, managing the import of system-related data.
This class represents a data structure for common metadata attributes associated with an entry, including flags for skipping, name, owner, group, file mode, and creation timestamp.

This class handles the processing of backup descriptors to restore database contents, acting as a SAX Content Handler. It manages the state of the restoration process, including transactions, URIs, and deferred permissions, while allowing subclasses to customize behavior for collections, resources, and deleted items.
This class manages deferred permission assignments for a specific database collection, ensuring that the correct owner, group, and mode are applied when permissions are eventually processed.
This class is responsible for logging restore-related messages at different severity levels (info, warn, error). It acts as an observer to capture and record events during a restore process.

This interface defines a set of methods that can be called to receive notifications about the progress and outcome of a restore operation, including starting, processing descriptors, creating collections, restoring resources, skipping resources, logging information, warnings, and errors, and signaling completion.

This abstract class provides default implementations for a listener that is notified of events during a backup restoration process, such as the start and end of the process, creation of collections, skipping resources, and the restoration of individual resources.
This class handles the processing of backup descriptors to restore database contents, acting as a SAX content handler.
This interface defines operations for applying deferred permissions to a database broker within a transaction, managing access control entries (ACEs) for specific targets.
This class defines and registers functions related to backup operations within the system, making them available for use.
This class provides functionality to list all available eXist backups within a specified directory and returns the list as an XML fragment.

This class is responsible for retrieving a specified zipped backup archive from a given directory and streaming its contents directly to an HTTP response, enforcing security by only allowing `.zip` files and requiring specific user roles and an active HTTP context.
This class implements a backup writer that serializes data into a zip archive, managing entries for collections, general content, and binary blobs.
This class provides a graphical user interface for creating a backup, allowing users to select a collection, specify a backup target, and choose whether to deduplicate blobs.
Manages the creation and identification of backup files within a specified directory, adhering to a defined naming convention that includes backup type (full or incremental) and a timestamp.
This class presents a dialog window for users to monitor the progress of a data restoration process, displaying messages, file counts, and transfer status.
This class provides an implementation for writing backup data to the file system, managing collections, entries, and their associated content and blob data.
Restores data from backup files to a database, managing application overwrites and providing progress updates.
This class handles the parsing of XML content, specifically counting the occurrences of 'resource' elements within a given namespace.
This class is responsible for counting the number of files described within an XML input stream.

This class represents a backup file, storing its associated file object and a timestamp derived from a formatted string, and provides methods to compare its date with other backup files or specific points in time.
This class aggregates warning and error messages generated during a restore service task, providing a consolidated view of all problems encountered.

This class serves as the main entry point for a command-line application, responsible for parsing arguments related to database operations such as backup and restore, and then orchestrating the execution of these operations.

This interface defines a callback mechanism for reporting the progress and status of a data collection or processing operation, including initiation, document processing, and error handling. Implementations can be interrupted, halting the process.

This class acts as a callback mechanism for processing collection data during a backup operation. It is responsible for exporting collection details and updating its progress, while also managing any errors encountered. It provides a way to retrieve the processed documents after the operation.

This class acts as a callback for processing documents during an export operation, handling the logic for including, potentially renaming, and serializing documents based on their export status and the presence of duplicates.
This class handles the processing of XML elements, specifically identifying and marking non-existent subcollections and resources as deleted.

This class provides functionality to export database contents, prioritizing data preservation even when encountering corrupted collections or unreadable documents. It can export descendant collections, place intact but orphaned documents into a special lost-and-found collection, and remove damaged documents detected by a consistency check. The exported data format is compatible with the standard backup tool.
This class describes a backup stored within a file system, allowing access to its contents and properties.
This class represents a specific type of error related to a resource, allowing for the inclusion of a document identifier alongside the error code, message, and an optional exception.
This class represents an error specific to a collection, storing an error code, message, and optionally an exception, along with the collection's ID and URI.
This class represents an error that occurs when an index is out of bounds, specifically associating the error with a document identifier.

This class serves as a base for reporting various types of errors within the system, encapsulating error codes, messages, and associated exceptions. It provides specific subclasses to detail errors related to resources, collections, and indices.
This interface defines a contract for creating and closing entries within a data archive, primarily used for backing up raw data files.
This class acts as a listener for the restoration service, providing visual feedback and progress updates to a graphical user interface dialog.
This class is responsible for executing a backup operation in a separate thread and then dismissing a dialog, with error logging for the backup process.

This class manages the process of backing up eXist-db content, including its structure, documents, and metadata, to a specified target location, with options for deduplicating blobs and handling graphical user interface interactions.

This interface defines a contract for writing backup data, abstracting the process of writing to various destinations such as directories or zip files, and managing entries and collections within the backup.
This class provides utility methods for managing test environments, including cleaning up database collections and data directories, reading files, and accessing the eXist home directory.
This enumeration defines a set of distinct states that a trigger can be in, representing its operational status.
This class encapsulates information about a scheduled job, providing details about its name, group, trigger, and firing schedule.
Represents a user-submitted job that executes an XQuery against the system, handling its execution context and resource.
This enum defines the distinct types of jobs that can be executed within the system: user-initiated jobs and system-generated jobs.
This class represents a job that can be scheduled by system tasks, ensuring only one instance runs at a time and queuing intersecting schedules.
This class is responsible for creating and initializing a Quartz scheduler, including its factory, and managing any exceptions that may occur during this process.
This class acts as a scheduler that manages and triggers various types of jobs, including startup, system, and user-defined tasks, using the Quartz scheduler library.
This class represents a task to asynchronously shut down a broker pool, ensuring existing operations can complete before termination.
This class represents a scheduled task designed to shut down the database, ensuring that the shutdown process is handled asynchronously to avoid blocking the scheduler.
This interface defines a contract for system tasks that are executable by a job scheduler, representing operations that need to be performed at scheduled times.
This enum defines a set of enumerated constants representing different actions to take when a job encounters an exception.
This class represents an exception that can be thrown during the execution of a job, and it provides mechanisms for cleaning up the job's state and controlling its subsequent execution or scheduling.

This interface defines a scheduler responsible for managing and executing various types of jobs, including startup, system, and user-defined tasks, with capabilities for periodic and cron-based scheduling, job lifecycle management, and configuration-driven job setup.

This abstract class serves as a base for user-defined jobs that can be scheduled and executed by a system. It defines a common group for these jobs and is intended to be extended by specific job implementations.
This class represents the configuration for a scheduled job, including its type, name, resource, scheduling details, and any associated parameters.
This abstract class provides a base for user-defined Java jobs that can be scheduled and executed by a job scheduler, handling the core execution logic and interaction with a broker pool.
